chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Safwan from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
It is appropriate for the Imam that his prayer be according to the weakest of those behind him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on how an Imam should pace his prayer relative to the congregation?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *takhfif* (leniency) for the Imam, ensuring that the congregation's diversity in capability is accommodated to maintain unity. Scholars emphasize that this rule prioritizes the comfort of the weakest follower (*da'if*) over the Imam's preference for lengthier recitation, thereby preventing *haraj* (hardship) and preserving the spiritual focus of the prayer.
